newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary breweries hit new highs after merger news.
newsitem.headline: Hungary breweries hit new highs after merger news.

text.p: The shares in Hungarian breweries Soproni Sorgyar and Martfu rose to new record highs on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday as trading resumed in them after their suspension on Thursday.

The BSE suspended trading in the two breweries for Thursday as the news that their majority shareholder, Austria's Brau Union announced the merger of its Hungarian units, were not available yet to a wide range of investors.
Sopron shares opened at 4,200 forints, up from Wednesday's close of 4,000 forints, also up from its previous high of 4,100 forints and jumped to a new record high of 4,350.
At 1107 GMT they stood at 4,300, up 300.
Martfu shares started the day steady at the previous record of 2,900 forints and advanced to a new high of 3,000 forints.
Both stocks had only a few hundred shares trade by 1135 GMT.

"Sopron's rise is evidently the result of the merger news," one trader said. "This is so despite the fact that only Sopron's preference shares are listed (on the BSE) while the merger refers to the ordinary stocks."

Brau Union announced Thursday morning a buyout offer to all Martfu shareholders at 206 Austrian schillings per share. This price exceeds the previous six months' weighted average price of 2,092 forints on the bourse by more than 43 percent.
During the merger process Martfu ordinary shares, listed on the BSE, will be converted into Sopron ordinary shares, which are not and will not be listed on the Budapest bourse.
